title: Analyze a shared-resource dilemma through different moral lenses

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Virtue asks what a good practical disposition would do; deontology examines duties; consequentialism compares outcomes; care attends to relationships and dependency. Rights ask whose protected claim is at stake; justice examines fair allocation. Natural-law approaches reason from accounts of human goods; religious ethics may also invoke revelation and tradition, interpreted differently. Particularism asks how a reason changes with context instead of assuming an exceptionless rule. These introductory questions do not exhaust any tradition.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Jo owns a camera and promised it to Rae Saturday 10–12. A community group requests it 11–13 for a useful event; another camera can be borrowed with a 30-minute trip by a willing organizer. Rae’s occasion cannot be repeated. Nobody has released Jo from the promise; no emergency exists.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Write one question from each framework, distinguish questions from conclusions, and defend an allocation under at least two lenses. Explain what new fact could alter it.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: The original borrower freely releases a promise; the new requester is the owner’s friend. Does friendship alone justify giving that requester preference over another equally eligible applicant?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: Keeping the promise has strong duty and relationship reasons; the group alternative reduces the consequence-based case for breaking it. Rights do not mean the owner has no obligations. Justice asks whether the alternative’s travel burden is fair. Particularism examines why an irreplaceable event differs from routine use. Partial: list labels without reasons. Incorrect: invent Rae’s consent. To deepen one lens, compare a primary argument and a serious objection, then revisit the same case before claiming expertise.
criteria: Competing reasons and limits remain visible

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Release removes that specific promise constraint, not the fairness question. State an allocation reason that survives exchanging names; relevant need or a previously accepted queue can matter. No single school label settles all facts.
criteria: Competing reasons and limits remain visible
